title: Open extension by zero and proper derived pushforward interchange
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $p:T\to B$ be a proper morphism of schemes and $i:V\hookrightarrow B$ a quasi-compact open immersion [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Form $T_V=T\times_BV$, with projections $b:T_V\to T$ and $p_V:T_V\to V$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. On the small etale sites, use the bounded-below derived categories of $\Lambda$-module sheaves and their derived direct images [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and degreewise extension by zero along open immersions [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. There is a natural isomorphism of functors
$$i_!\circ Rp_{V,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*\circ b_!:D^+((T_V)_{\Et},\Lambda)\longrightarrow D^+(B_{\Et},\Lambda).$$

source.place: Tag 0F7B, label lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, Cartesian open-immersion specialization, case (a) or (b)

proof.text: Apply the existing proper/open interchange theorem [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] to the Cartesian square with top-left $T_V$, top-right $T$, bottom-left $V$, bottom-right $B$, horizontal open immersions $b$ and $i$, and proper vertical maps $p_V$ and $p$. Its hypotheses hold because $i$ is quasi-compact open (hence an open immersion), $b$ is its base change and therefore an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], and $p_V$ is the base change of the proper morphism $p$ and hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The theorem supplies a canonical natural isomorphism $i_!Rp_{V,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*b_!$ on the bounded-below derived categories of finite commutative-ring etale module sheaves, exactly the asserted functor isomorphism.
